text: dsh-subagent-progress 是 DeepSeek Harness 网页端插件，在会话输入框上方显示子代理状态面板。主机端把子代理会话事件折叠为进度投影，并为子代理注册 notify_user 状态汇报工具；网页端展示轮次、步骤、最近工具动作、助手预览、汇报和失败信息。用户可查看子代理会话并在卡片上暂停或重试。适合同时运行多个子代理、希望在主会话中掌握进展的用户。无需额外 API 密钥或账号。

dsh-subagent-progress is a DeepSeek Harness web plugin that shows subagent turns, actions, updates, and failures above the conversation composer. It also lets users open, pause, or retry a child session. No extra API key or account is required.
想在主会话里直接看到各个子代理正在做什么
能不能把子代理的步骤、工具动作和进度汇报放在输入框附近
Show me live status updates from my child agents in the web conversation.
dsh-subagent-progress 的功能「子代理状态面板」：在网页会话输入框上方显示子代理轮次、步骤、最近工具动作、助手内容预览和状态汇报；有子代理活动时出现，方便从主会话查看进展。
dsh-subagent-progress 的功能「子代理卡片操作」：在网页状态卡片上可打开子代理会话，并对运行或失败的子代理执行暂停或重试；操作通过客户端的 remote.subagents 服务触发。

dsh-subagent-progress README · What you see：- **One card per running subagent**: label, turn/step, todo completion (`1/3`), the exact action in flight (`bash: cargo build --release`, not a bare tool name), and elapsed time.
- **Subagents report in their own words**: one-sentence updates about progress, how long remains, and key discoveries — brand blue = progress, amber = ETA, green = finding (all sourced from DS theme variables, light/dark adaptive).
- **Stall alerts**: a live subagent silent for 5+ minutes turns its status dot amber.
- **Failure actions**: when a subagent's turn dies (e.g. a 429 overload), its card stays — red dot, the distilled error on one line (hover for the full text), and explicit actions: **Retry** queues a fresh turn for the child right from the card, **Open** jumps into its session; a running card likewise gets a **Pause** button that interrupts the active turn (handy during retry storms).
- **Aligned at any count**: cards snap into an equal-width grid with a uniform four-row structure, so they line up perfectly whether there are two or ten; beyond two rows the panel scrolls instead of eating your screen.

dsh-subagent-progress README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-subagent-progress
```

Then restart `dsh web`. Published on npm as [dsh-subagent-progress](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-subagent-progress). Requires dsh ≥ 0.1.2-rc.1 — see [Compatibility](#compatibility).

dsh-subagent-progress README · Usage：- **Click a card** → open that subagent's full session.
- **Hover the update area** → a frosted popover shows the full update, markdown-rendered (lists and code blocks intact).
- No configuration needed — install and it works.

dsh-subagent-progress README · How it works (30-second version)：- **Passive observation**: every subagent's session events (turns, steps, tool calls, assistant text) are folded into a small progress state that dsh's projection framework **pushes to every browser automatically** — so there is always progress on the card, even if the model never says a word.
- **Active reporting**: every subagent gets a `notify_user` tool plus guidance to report in single sentences (and a gentle reminder after 6 consecutive tool calls without one). Each report is an ordinary event in the child's durable session log, carried out by the same channel — persistent and replayable by construction.
dsh-subagent-progress README · How it works (30-second version)：No dsh source is modified; the host half works in any deployment, the UI half renders only under dsh web.

dsh-subagent-progress README · Compatibility：Official dsh plugins declare their version contract as `peerDependencies` on the `@deepseek-ai/*` core packages they touch; this plugin follows the same convention. All core packages ship in lockstep release trains (0.1.x-rc), so one range covers the whole host.

**Supported: dsh ≥ 0.1.2-rc.1, < 0.2.0. Developed and live-verified on 0.1.5-rc.1.**

The floor is not arbitrary — it comes from the exact API surface this plugin uses, checked against the published tarballs of every core release:

dsh-subagent-progress README · Compatibility：| API surface we use | Provided by | Introduced |
|---|---|---|
| `remote.subagents` wire API (`prompt` / `interruptByParent`, `mode: 'continuable'`) — the Retry/Pause buttons | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-remotes` | **0.1.2-rc.1** (absent in 0.1.0-rc.8) |
| `sessionProjections` service (server-side event folding) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection` | ≤ 0.1.0-rc.8 |
| `systemPrompt` service (reporting guidance section) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` | ≤ 0.1.0-rc.8 |
| `defineTool` (`notify_user` registration) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` | ≤ 0.1.0-rc.8 |
| Client services `sessions` / `slots` / `locale` / `remote` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` | ≤ 0.1.0-rc.8 |

dsh-subagent-progress README · Compatibility：Because the web client declares `remote.subagents` in its cordis `inject`, the whole dock — not just the buttons — requires ≥ 0.1.2-rc.1. Versions 0.1.2 through 0.1.3 are expected to work by API surface but are not continuously tested; 0.1.5-rc.1 is the version every release is verified against.

dsh-subagent-progress README · Compatibility：One nuance on enforcement: npm semver cannot express "any prerelease train from X onward" — a range like `>=0.1.2-rc.1 <0.2.0` only admits the 0.1.2-rc.* line under the same-tuple prerelease rule, and `^0.1.5-rc.1` pins a single train (which is why official plugins redeclare peers every train). Since neither expresses the real contract, this section is the authoritative statement; `peerDependencies` stays minimal (`cordis`, `dsh-tools`), matching the official client-plugin convention.
